A_target.statement:
There exists a [[Definition:Stochastic Process|stochastic process]] $\sequence {B_t}_{t \mathop \ge 0}$ such that:
:$B_0 = 0$
:$t \mapsto B_t$ is [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]]
:for $s < t$, $B_t - B_s \sim \map N {0, t - s}$ is [[Definition:Independent Random Variables|independent]] of $\set {B_u: u \le s}$
That is, [[Definition:Brownian Motion|Brownian motion]] exists.

B_source.statement:
Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be [[Definition:Independent Identically Distributed|i.i.d.]] with $\map \Pr {X_i = 1} = \map \Pr {X_i = -1} = \dfrac 1 2$.
The [[Definition:Simple Random Walk|simple symmetric random walk]] is:
:$\displaystyle S_n = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i$

object_map.reformulation: The discrete walk must first be embedded as a continuous-time path by linear interpolation between steps, so that both objects live in the same function space.

validity_conditions: the walk increments must have mean zero and finite variance for the diffusive scaling to be the right one
tightness of the rescaled paths in the space of continuous functions is required, not just convergence of finite-dimensional marginals
proof_plan:
Define the rescaled, linearly interpolated walk:
:$W^{\paren n}_t = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt n} S_{\floor {n t} } + \dfrac {n t - \floor {n t} } {\sqrt n} X_{\floor {n t} + 1}$

For $0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_k$, the increments of $W^{\paren n}$ are independent sums of i.i.d. steps.
By the [[Central Limit Theorem]], $W^{\paren n}_t - W^{\paren n}_s \to \map N {0, t - s}$ in [[Definition:Convergence in Distribution|distribution]].
From moment bounds on increments and [[Prohorov's Theorem]], the laws of $W^{\paren n}$ on $\map C {\closedint 0 1}$ are [[Definition:Tight Family of Measures|tight]].

Tightness together with convergence of [[Definition:Finite-Dimensional Distribution|finite-dimensional distributions]] gives [[Definition:Weak Convergence of Measures|weak convergence]] to a limit process $B$ with the required increment law.
This is [[Donsker's Theorem]].

As the limit law is supported on $\map C {\closedint 0 1}$, $B$ has [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] sample paths.
{{qed}}
